title: The Art of the Short with Lakshmi Ganapathi: FICO, DoorDash, and AeroVironment
summary: Ganapathi presents shorts in FICO, AeroVironment and DoorDash. Eisman remains short FICO, accepts its competitive threat, and finds the delivery credit-risk argument compelling. Primary evidence supports FICO debt-funded repurchases and expanding VantageScore adoption. It contradicts the asserted national BNPL prevalence and the categorical claim that AeroVironment has been priced out of its market. Numerous valuation, legal and product-comparison premises remain unverified; general BNPL statistics do not establish DoorDash customer exposure.
assessment: The most substantiated thesis is erosion of FICO exclusivity and increased leverage. DoorDash and AeroVironment theses rely on unverified exposure, customer economics and product equivalence. Eisman explicitly adopts several claims in the close, while his position disclosures remain distinct from price targets.
speaker_map_notes: SPEAKER_01 identifies himself as Eisman and introduces Lakshmi Ganapathi of Unicus Research; SPEAKER_00 answers as Ganapathi. Interjections are resolved from dialogue.
framework_points: Classify shorts by structural competition, product economics and credit exposure.
Separate poor contractor economics from company profitability.
Look beyond filings to product quality, warranties and management behavior.
Monitor debt-funded buybacks and acquisition accounting.
Require matching denominators before inferring customer dependence.
tools_and_charts: FICO mortgage score prices and market share
Goodwill as a share of assets and impairment charges
BNPL adoption and grocery or delivery use
transcript_cautions: Nova Credit appears as NOAA Credit.
June fiscal third quarter is clarified after confusion between Q2 and Q3.
VantageScore application share, securitization share and overall scoring share are mixed in the dialogue.
European exposure percentage lacks a clear denominator.
At 1961-2016 captions omit transitions between the AeroVironment and DoorDash classifications; closing summary clarifies intended meaning.
Eisman closing statement converts general BNPL population statistics into a claim about DoorDash customers without supporting platform data.
